key_insight: Device retention time varies substantially across lines, drains, and airway devices, suggesting that duration patterns can be meaningfully characterized by device category.
clinical_relevance: Understanding which device types tend to remain in place longer may help support safer device management and reduce risks linked to prolonged exposure, such as infection or tissue injury.
method: Exploratory analysis of patient lines, drains, and airways (LDA) electronic health record data
Machine learning used to separate short vs prolonged device retention
Compared duration distributions and patterns across device categories
evidence_signal: The study analyzed observational EHR data across multiple patient encounters and found distinct duration patterns among device groups.
watch_item: Because the study is observational and based on existing EHR data, findings may reflect documentation and practice variation and should not be treated as proof of causation.
paper_title: AI-Driven Analysis of Device Duration in Anesthesiology
